The presence of a well-circumscribed, yellowish mass in the right lower lobe on macroscopic examination and the composition of fibroblasts, collagen, and inflammatory cells on microscopic examination also support this diagnosis. The diagnostic differences between lung cancer and other candidate diseases, such as bronchiectasis and pulmonary tuberculosis, further confirm this diagnosis.

However, the presence of bloody sputum and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate are more suggestive of lung cancer. The diagnostic differences between bronchiectasis and lung cancer, such as the presence of clubbing of the digits in bronchiectasis, also support lung cancer as the more likely diagnosis.
